emma (Support): :rotating_light: Escalation from AcmeCorp — their payment webhook endpoint started returning 403s around 15:10 UTC after our NAT rebalance. Customer says they haven't changed allowlist. Ticket INC-4023. Can netops/infra take a look?

raj (AcmeCorp): We're seeing ~30% of webhook posts rejected with 403. IPs in our logs: 54.12.34.50 previously, now we see 54.12.34.78 and 54.12.34.79. We only allowlist a very small /28. Please advise urgently.

kevin (Netops): Looking. Which region/VPC and any maintenance windows?

emma (Support): us-east-1 private VPC. We did a NAT pool rebalance/autoscale at 14:58 UTC — rolling SNAT reassignment. I attached app logs in the ticket.

sophia (Infra): Quick ask: paste the request trace id so we can match on our side. Also ask them to run: `curl -v -H "X-Trace: <id>" https://hooks.acme.example/webhook` to surface headers.

raj (AcmeCorp): Trace id: trace_0a3b. From our side `curl -v` returns 403 and header shows `x-client-ip: 54.12.34.79`. Snippet: ```HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden\nServer: nginx\nx-client-ip: 54.12.34.79\ncontent-type: application/json\n{ \"error\": \"IP not allowlisted\" }```

kevin (Netops): Netops note: our SNAT pool expanded into a new small block (54.12.34.64/29) last night during autoscale. Some flows are now egressing from those newly allocated addresses. Looks like the customer's firewall is narrower than our pool. Two mitigation paths: 1) ask customer to add the new addresses/range to their allowlist, or 2) move them to static/reserved egress (Dedicated) or enable temporary SNAT pinning for their project.

emma (Support): Customer prefers not to modify firewall rules quickly. Any short-term options from infra? Can we pin egress IPs per project?

sophia (Infra): We support sticky SNAT (pinning) for customers using the reserved-egress feature; for Hosted Private it's off by default. Short-term we can enable pinning for a project for a few hours as a workaround (requires ops action). Alternatively, provide a precise list of current active SNAT IPs for them to allowlist.

kevin (Netops): I'll verify with packet logs. Example debug: `tcpdump -nni eth0 host 54.12.34.79` and check our allocation logs. I can see `ALLOC SNAT 54.12.34.79 -> eni-0abc` at 14:56:48 UTC, so that IP was assigned during the rolling update.

raj (AcmeCorp): If you can confirm the exact addresses we should add, we'll push the firewall change. Also flagged a couple TLS handshake resets earlier — any correlation?

sophia (Infra): TLS chain hasn't changed (same certs). The handshake resets likely came from transient ENI failovers during the rebalance. Primary issue is IP mismatch with their allowlist. I'll compile the active SNAT set now.

kevin (Netops): Exporting allocations, example command and result shown for ops: ```for ip in $(cat /proc/nat_allocs); do echo $ip; done``` # result: 54.12.34.50,54.12.34.64,54.12.34.65,54.12.34.66,54.12.34.67,54.12.34.68,54.12.34.69,54.12.34.70,54.12.34.79

emma (Support): Raj — temporary list to add (stopgap): 54.12.34.50, 54.12.34.64-54.12.34.70, 54.12.34.79. We're also preparing to enable SNAT pinning for your project until you finish the firewall update. I'll log the change and ETA.

raj (AcmeCorp): We will add those to our allowlist and confirm once deployed. Please enable pinning so we see stability while we roll that ACL change.

emma (Support): :thumbsup: Assigning to kevin to enable SNAT pinning and to sophia to confirm export of the final active IP list. Updating INC-4023 with steps and temporary workaround. ETA for pinning ~15:40 UTC.

kevin (Netops): Running pin command for the project: `redwood netops snat-pin --project acmecorp --duration 4h`. Kicking off now. Will post confirmation.
\egress-rotation-bot: SNAT pinning completed for project=acmecorp duration=4h assigned_ips=54.12.34.50,54.12.34.64,54.12.34.65,54.12.34.66

raj (AcmeCorp): Confirming — our webhook traces for trace_0a3b now show 200 OK. Thanks for the quick turnaround.

emma (Support): Closing loop in this thread: follow-up actions — (1) customer to update firewall rules permanently (recommend reserved egress or expanded CIDR), (2) postmortem note on incident board about SNAT rebalance communications, (3) consider flagging projects with tight allowlists before autoscale rebalances. Marking INC-4023 for follow-up. :white_check_mark:
